The coronavirus will weigh on near-term activity and raise downside risks, but the FOMC’s move to the effective lower bound, large-scale Treasury and agency MBS purchases, expanded repos, discount window easing, and global dollar swap lines are consistent with the credit-channel literature (Bernanke–Gertler; Gertler and Gilchrist; Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein; Oliner and Rudebusch) in reducing external finance premia and supporting cash-flow constrained firms and households. With market-based inflation compensation falling while surveys are steadier, the easing stance aligns with inflation-targeting and expectations frameworks (Svensson; Sims; Romer and Romer) to anchor the symmetric 2% objective and mitigate deflation and liquidity-trap risks. Net: still negative near term, but partially offset by aggressive, literature-supported policy tools.
